# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 90 (Bu-Vb Pc90)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc90
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 90
**Title (English, from literature):** Making an oversize itch cloth

**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kaṇḍuppaṭicchādi-sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 90) is a monastic training rule in the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka regulating the permissible size of an itch cloth or medicated bandage (*kaṇḍuppaṭicchādi*) [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a monk who makes an itch cloth exceeding the prescribed dimensions must have it cut down to size and confess an expiation offense (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this rule was shared across nearly all early Buddhist vinaya lineages [SuttaCentral]. In the Pali tradition, it corresponds to Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Pācittiya 90 and Parivāra Pācittiya 90, as well as the parallel rule for nuns (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 165) [SuttaCentral]. External parallels are preserved in the Sarvāstivāda (Chinese and Sanskrit Bu Vb/Pm Pc 88), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit versions for monks and nuns), Mahīśāsaka (Chinese Bu Vb/Pm Pc 88), Mahāsāṅghika and Lokottaravāda (Chinese and Sanskrit Bu Pm Pc 87 and Bi Vb/Pm Pc 67), Dharmaguptaka (Chinese Bu Vb/Pm Pc 88), and Kāśyapīya traditions [SuttaCentral]. In DharmaNexus text-reuse matches, the rule shares substantial formulaic prose with neighboring Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga rules governing robe measurements and materials, including Pācittiya 89 (§0.1–1.16), Pācittiya 91 (§0.1–2.21), Pācittiya 87, Pācittiya 88, and Pācittiya 92, along with several Nissaggiya Pācittiya rules (Np 11, 13, 14, 15) and sub-commentarial texts such as the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
